treatments.name: Mental health treatment plan (Better Access)
treatments.notes: From a GP, psychiatrist or paediatrician. Medicare rebates for 10 individual and 10 group sessions per calendar year with a psychologist, social worker or occupational therapist. Medicare usually covers part of the fee.

treatments.name: Psychiatrist
treatments.notes: Medicare rebates with a referral, usually from a GP.

treatments.name: rTMS for depression
treatments.notes: On the MBS since 1 November 2021 (items 14216, 14217, 14219, 14220) for adults over 18 with major depressive disorder who have tried at least two classes of antidepressants and remain unwell, and have not had rTMS before. Prescribed by an rTMS-trained psychiatrist, with a referral from a GP or psychiatrist. First course up to 35 sessions, retreatment course up to 15.

programs.name: My Aged Care
programs.notes: Covers the Commonwealth Home Support Program (entry-level help at home, including transport providers) and Support at Home.

programs.name: Mobility Allowance (Services Australia)
programs.notes: Help with travel costs for some people who cannot use public transport. See the website for who can get it.

programs.name: DVA
programs.notes: Veteran Card holders can get help with travel to medical treatment, including Booked Car with Driver.

facts.text: Your heart beats around 100,000 times every day, about 72 beats a minute at rest.
Most adults need 7 to 9 hours of sleep a night to feel their best.
Babies are born with about 270 bones. Many fuse as we grow, leaving 206 in adults.
Your brain is only about 2% of your body weight, but uses about 20% of its energy.
Australia's guidelines suggest adults aim for 2½ to 5 hours of moderate activity, like brisk walking, each week.
Breaking up long stretches of sitting, even just by standing and moving for a few minutes, is good for your health.
Australian Dietary Guidelines suggest most adults eat 5 serves of vegetables and 2 serves of fruit a day.
facts.source: Eat For Health: Australian Dietary Guidelines

facts.text: Water makes up around 60% of an adult's body weight.
Your skin is your body's largest organ.
At rest, most adults take 12 to 20 breaths a minute: well over 17,000 breaths a day.
Red blood cells live for about 120 days before your body recycles them.
Your body makes more than 2 million new red blood cells every second.
In Australia, sunlight on the skin is the main source of vitamin D.
The smallest bone in your body, the stapes, is in your middle ear and is only about 3 mm long.
Your thigh bone, the femur, is the longest and strongest bone in your body.
Fingernails grow about 3 mm a month.
Hair on your head grows about 1 to 1.5 cm a month.
Most people blink around 15 to 20 times a minute, which keeps the eyes moist and clean.
More than 2 in 5 Australians aged 16 to 85 have had a mental health condition at some point in their life. You are far from alone.
facts.source: ABS: National Study of Mental Health and Wellbeing

facts.text: Regular physical activity can lift your mood and help you sleep better.
If you take several medicines, your GP can refer you for a free Home Medicines Review, where a pharmacist checks they all work safely together.
Unwanted or expired medicines can be returned to any pharmacy in Australia for free, safe disposal.
A Home Medicines Review pharmacist can also suggest ways to help you remember to take the right medicine at the right time.
The cells lining your stomach are replaced every few days.
Your liver can regrow after part of it has been removed.
Going to bed and getting up at the same times each day, even on weekends, helps your body clock and your sleep.
Your small intestine is several metres long, folded up to fit inside your abdomen.
Taste bud cells are replaced about every one to two weeks.
A mental health treatment plan from your GP gives Medicare rebates for up to 10 individual sessions a year with a psychologist or other mental health professional.
Staying connected with friends and family, and making time for things you enjoy, are simple ways to look after your mental health.
facts.source: healthdirect: Tips for good mental health
